name: Exchange Law for Signed Minimal Nonfaces
statement: Let ample $H=H(\Sigma,\boldsymbol\sigma)$ arise from an admissible signing of the minimal nonfaces of $\Sigma$. For $a\notin H$, let $\mathcal V_H(a)$ be the minimal nonfaces on which $a$ realizes the omitted signed trace. For $c\in H$, let $\mathcal R_H(a,c)$ be those minimal nonfaces on which $a$ and $c$ differ and $c$ is the unique old representative of its trace. Then $(H\setminus\{c\})\cup\{a\}$ is ample with shattered complex $\Sigma$ exactly when $\mathcal V_H(a)=\mathcal R_H(a,c)$. The new signing pivots each violated clause to $c$'s trace and leaves every other clause unchanged. Moreover $H\cup\{a\}$ is ample exactly when $|\mathcal V_H(a)|=1$; in that case its shattered complex is $\Sigma$ together with that unique newly shattered support.
proof: On each minimal nonface, the old projection omits exactly its signed trace. After exchanging $c$ for $a$, it still omits one trace precisely when either $a$ fills the old omission and $c$ was the sole representative of a different trace, or $a$ does not fill it and removing $c$ creates no second omission. Simultaneous validity is exactly the displayed set equality and gives the signing pivot. The exchanged family has $|\Sigma|$ concepts and shadow contained in $\Sigma$, so Sandwich equality forces ampleness and the exact shadow. For addition, every violated clause becomes shattered. Ampleness allows exactly one new support; conversely, if exactly one clause is violated, any newly shattered support must equal that minimal nonface, so the enlarged family again meets Sandwich equality.
